question: What is the main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To identify health problems and community resources
options.B: To punish communities for poor hygiene practices
options.C: To treat individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: To replace the national census data collection

explanation: A community diagnosis evaluates overall health needs and available resources to guide future interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is a community diagnosis compared to examining an individual patient?

options.A: Both focus exclusively on surgical interventions
options.B: Both deal with only one person at a time
options.C: Both require a stethoscope and a laboratory blood test
options.D: Both processes aim to uncover health deficits before planning treatment

explanation: Assessment must precede intervention whether dealing with a single person or an entire population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is resource allocation a critical step following a community diagnosis?

options.A: Healthcare resources are limited and must be directed where needed most
options.B: Surplus funds must be spent quickly before the financial year ends
options.C: Government policy requires spending equal amounts in every village
options.D: International donors demand strict financial auditing of local clinics

explanation: Scarcity of funds and materials requires targeted distribution based on actual identified needs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h2)

question: A local clinic has fifty malaria rapid test kits left. How does community diagnosis help use them?

options.A: Handing them out randomly at the weekly market
options.B: Directing kits to the ward with the highest fever incidence
options.C: Saving them in the main office for unexpected visitors
options.D: Distributing them evenly among healthy school teachers

explanation: Data from a community diagnosis ensures scarce supplies target populations with the highest risk. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary benefit of involving local community members in health assessments?

options.A: It removes the need for trained public health nurses
options.B: It ensures the government does not pay staff salaries
options.C: It stops all infectious diseases within one month
options.D: It fosters a sense of ownership over health outcomes

explanation: Active participation ensures locals value and maintain the health programs introduced in their area. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: How does community participation change the role of community members in healthcare?

options.A: From paid hospital workers to independent supervisors
options.B: From tax payers to international health donors
options.C: From sick patients to licensed medical doctors
options.D: From passive recipients to active partners in health

explanation: Involving the community changes their status from people who just receive help to those who help design it. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: What type of data does a community diagnosis provide for health policy makers?

options.A: Empirical evidence on morbidity, mortality, and hazards
options.B: Personal opinions of international political leaders
options.C: Financial statements of private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Historical records of colonial missionary activities

explanation: Policy formulation requires factual data regarding disease rates and environmental risks within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why must public health planning avoid relying purely on guesswork?

options.A: It prevents nurses from administering routine immunizations
options.B: It leads to misallocation of scarce resources and ineffective programs
options.C: It violates international trade agreements on medical equipment
options.D: It automatically increases the cost of building new hospitals

explanation: Guesswork results in programs that do not address the actual problems facing the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: What function does the initial community diagnosis serve for future health programs?

options.A: It replaces the need for any future clinic records
options.B: It acts as a permanent legal contract for funding
options.C: It provides a baseline to measure future progress
options.D: It guarantees zero disease outbreaks in the future

explanation: Initial data offers a baseline measurement to compare against future health status assessments. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is periodic re-assessment necessary in community health management?

options.A: To measure whether health interventions are improving the community
options.B: To prove that nurses are working overtime without pay
options.C: To satisfy the personal curiosity of visiting politicians
options.D: To increase the population size of the rural settlement

explanation: Repeating assessments helps track changes in health indices over time to evaluate program success. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)
